title: Sift: inbox triage and plain-English labels
one_liner: A Gmail-style inbox of 500 synthetic emails. Type an intent, get a label. Run a fixed 7-dimension triage pass that sorts the inbox into lanes and shows where keyword rules fail.
what_it_does: The page shows a Gmail-faithful inbox with 500 deterministic synthetic emails (seed 20260917) plus 21 hand-written traps. The user presses `/` and types an intent such as "customers threatening to cancel". The server fans out one yes/no judgment per email and streams match probabilities back as NDJSON. Code applies the label at probability >= 0.5, marks 0.5 to 0.8 as borderline, filters the inbox to matches, and sorts rows by match probability when the run ends. Several labels AND together with no new inference. A menu item "Triage inbox" runs seven fixed judgments per email in one request: category, needs reply, urgency, sentiment, phishing, churn, refund. Code computes a priority score from slider weights, routes each email to a lane (Priority, Needs review under 0.7 category confidence, FYI, Spam), and surfaces phishing at the top. A keyword-rule baseline runs in the browser; a "Rules != Jev" lane lists disagreements with the full body so the user sees who is right. A HUD shows judged count, elapsed time, p50/p95 latency, tokens and cost. Keyboard: j/k move, e archive, r toggle reply flag, b toggle rules.

jev_questions.instructions: Read `email.subject` and `email.body`. Which single category best describes what this email is primarily about? Judge the sender's actual purpose, not incidental words.
options: billing: A customer's charges, invoices, payments, duplicate charges, refunds or subscription pricing problems
bug: A customer reports that a product feature is broken, erroring, down, slow or behaving incorrectly
feature_request: A customer asks for new functionality or an improvement that does not exist yet
sales_lead: A prospect or existing customer wants to buy, upgrade, get a quote, book a demo or discuss a contract
security: Security alerts, suspected account compromise, vulnerability reports, suspicious logins, 2FA or credential problems
legal_privacy: Legal notices, GDPR/CCPA data requests, data deletion, subpoenas, DPA or terms questions
spam_marketing: Unsolicited marketing, cold sales outreach, promotional newsletters, phishing, scams or impersonation attempts from outside senders
internal: A coworker writing from our own company domain (northwind.cloud) about operations, meetings, HR, IT, planning or team logistics
other: Anything that fits none of the above, e.g. thank-you notes, offboarding/export requests, misdirected mail, community or press requests

jev_questions.instructions: Does the sender of `email` expect a human at our company to write back? Mass mailings, automated notifications, newsletters and marketing blasts do not expect a reply.
options: true: A specific person is waiting for an answer, decision or confirmation from us
false: No reply is expected: automated, informational, bulk or marketing message

jev_questions.instructions: How quickly does this email need action from our team, based on the real situation the sender describes (ignore sarcastic or ironic framing and marketing pressure tactics like fake deadlines)?
options: Can wait a week
This week
Today
Right now
jev_questions.state_shape: { email: { from, subject, body } }; answer.score is 0..3 probability-weighted

jev_questions.instructions: What is the sender's actual emotional tone toward our company? Read past politeness formulas and sarcasm to the underlying attitude.
options: Friendly
Neutral
Frustrated
Furious
jev_questions.state_shape: { email: { from, subject, body } }; answer.score is 0..3

jev_questions.instructions: Is this email a phishing attempt or scam: does it try to trick the recipient into clicking a suspicious link, entering credentials, paying a fake invoice, buying gift cards, or acting on a fake authority (fake CEO, fake bank, fake vendor)?
options: true: Deceptive message designed to steal credentials, money or data
false: Legitimate message from who it claims to be, including pushy or fear-based marketing and cold sales pitches that only ask for a meeting or a purchase from a real company

jev_questions.instructions: Does the sender say they are cancelling, will cancel, are switching to a competitor, or are seriously considering leaving our product or service?
options: true: The sender themselves is cancelling, leaving or threatening to leave
false: No cancellation or churn intent from the sender (mentions of cancellation in marketing copy, newsletters or someone else's story do not count)

jev_questions.instructions: Does the sender ask our company to refund, reverse or credit back money they paid?
options: true: The sender wants their money back or a credit for a charge
false: No request for money back (a refund mentioned in marketing text or a policy description does not count)

jev_questions.instructions: An inbox operator wants to find emails that match this description: "${intent}". Read `email.from`, `email.subject` and `email.body`. Does this email genuinely match the description, judged by what the sender actually means and intends rather than by surface keywords?
options: true: The email clearly fits the operator's description
false: The email does not fit the description, or only mentions related words in passing, sarcastically, in quoted history or in marketing copy
jev_questions.state_shape: { email: { from, subject, body } }; intent is free text, max 200 chars; SUGGESTED_INTENTS in src/lib/labels.ts

request_cadence: Triage: one request per email carrying all 7 questions, 12 in flight, 500 requests per pass (~5.3 s, ~100 req/s). Label: one request per email per intent, 12 in flight, 500 requests per intent (~5.5 s). Streamed back as NDJSON; UI batches updates every 50 ms.

dm1_mapping.notes: Map results[i].label -> category, results[i].confidence -> categoryConfidence (needsHuman threshold 0.7 unchanged), results[i].scores -> categoryProbabilities. Label descriptions carry the instruction; keep the northwind.cloud domain in the internal description.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"texts":[...32 emails], "statement":"The sender expects a person at our company to write back.", "when_true":"A specific person waits for an answer, decision or confirmation from us.", "when_false":"Automated, bulk, newsletter or marketing message; no reply expected."}

POST /rate {"texts":[...32 emails], "scale":["Can wait a week: no real deadline, or the sender says there is no rush","This week: a real request that should be handled within days","Today: the sender is blocked or losing money and needs action today","Right now: production is down, a live incident or a security breach; act immediately. Ignore sarcastic framing and fake marketing deadlines"]}
dm1_mapping.notes: score is 0..1; store urgency = score * 3 so priority.ts and rules.ts comparisons stay unchanged. confidence -> urgencyConfidence (max of scores).

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /rate {"texts":[...32 emails], "scale":["Friendly: warm, thankful or positive toward our company","Neutral: matter-of-fact, no strong feeling","Frustrated: annoyed, disappointed or sarcastic under polite wording","Furious: angry, insulting, threatening or shouting"]}
dm1_mapping.notes: sentiment = score * 3. Read past politeness formulas: put that in the Frustrated description, since there is no instruction field.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"texts":[...32 emails], "statement":"This email is a phishing attempt or a scam.", "when_true":"It tries to steal credentials, money or data: fake login link, fake invoice, gift cards, fake CEO, bank or vendor.", "when_false":"A real company writing as itself, including pushy or fear-based marketing and cold sales pitches that only ask for a meeting or purchase."}
dm1_mapping.notes: Include From line in the text so lookalike domains such as micros0ft-secure.com are visible.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"texts":[...32 emails], "statement":"The sender is cancelling, switching to a competitor or seriously considering leaving.", "when_true":"The sender themselves says they will cancel, leave or switch.", "when_false":"No churn intent from the sender; the word cancel in marketing copy, a newsletter or someone else's story does not count."}

POST /yes-no {"texts":[...32 emails], "statement":"The sender asks us to refund, reverse or credit back money they paid.", "when_true":"The sender wants their money back or a credit for a charge.", "when_false":"No request for money back; a refund mentioned in marketing text or a policy description does not count."}

POST /yes-no {"texts":[...32 emails], "statement":"This email matches the description: <intent>.", "when_true":"What the sender actually means and intends fits the description.", "when_false":"It does not fit, or only mentions related words in passing, sarcastically, in quoted history or in marketing copy."}
dm1_mapping.notes: For the 10 SUGGESTED_INTENTS ship hand-written declaratives instead of the template, e.g. "customers threatening to cancel" -> statement "The sender threatens to cancel or leave."; "someone asking for a refund" -> "The sender asks for a refund."; "production is down or broken for them" -> "The sender reports that the product is down or broken for them."; "phishing or a scam" -> "This email is a phishing attempt or a scam."; "sarcastic or passive-aggressive tone" -> "The sender is sarcastic or passive-aggressive."; "newsletters I can ignore" -> "This is a newsletter that needs no reply.". Free text falls back to the template; 200 char cap stays.

risks: Throughput drops from ~100 req/s to 2 req/s. The original story is 500 emails in 5 s; the port must reframe it as batches of 32 with a visible progress bar, or the demo feels slow.
Seven separate routes replace one 7-question request. A row is complete only after all seven batch calls; partial judgments must render without breaking priority.ts (guard on undefined).
Token budget: 500 emails x ~250 tokens x 7 routes is ~875k tokens per full pass, close to the 1M tokens/min org limit shared by all visitors. Default to 128 emails.
rate score is 0..1 weighted position; multiply by 3 or every threshold in priority.ts and rules.ts (urgency < 1, off-by-one-level disagreements) silently breaks.

No instruction field on classify/rate: the nuance in the Jev instructions (ignore sarcasm, ignore fake deadlines) must live inside label and scale descriptions and needs a probe run on the 21 traps to confirm.
Free-text intents become a templated statement, which is longer than the ideal short declarative; quality on unusual intents may be lower than the hand-written suggested ones.
yes-no hints are shared per batch, so the four boolean statements cannot share one request; each needs its own call.
Trap fixture references northwind.cloud as the company domain; keep that string in the internal label description or internal classification breaks.
